daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Indonesian police are actively hunting those who ordered the wiretapping of President Prabowo, with the intelligence chief warning the surveillance may amount to treason. The scandal has drawn public attention toward former President Jokowi, prompting questions about why scrutiny has focused on the previous administration. The DPR will wait until after recess to assess the dynamics surrounding a proposed wiretapping law, with commentators noting the scandal serves as an alarm for the need for such legislation.

  • Golkar party has denied circulating rumors that an extraordinary national congress (munaslub) will be held soon, and the party has ordered its cadres to upload content on social media, learning from Minister Bahlil's approach.
  • The government and DPR have decided to convert part-time PPPK (government contract workers) including teachers, firefighters, and health workers to full-time status, with CPNS recruitment to open in November and age limits potentially relaxed.
  • The Attorney General's Office has deepened its investigation into alleged bribery by an illegal nickel mining company to state officials, having seized Rp 11.79 billion and now pursuing a figure identified as "AK."
  • The new Labor Protection Law stipulates that decent living needs will help determine the provincial minimum wage (UMP), and fixed-term employment contracts (PKWT) will be capped at four years, while joint leave will not reduce annual leave entitlements.
  • The National Board for Waqf (BGN) head Sudaryono has explained the rationale for recruiting KPK officials to the agency, and stated that supervisors' salaries will not be affected by the maximum operational cost cap for MBG.
  • Former President Jokowi, along with his sons Gibran and Kaesang, attended the wedding reception of Gusti Sura and KPH FX Adimas at Pura Mangkunegaran in Solo.
  • MPR Deputy Speaker Fadli Zon has expressed appreciation for foreigners and diaspora who advance Indonesian culture.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo received credentials from 11 foreign envoys and pushed for stronger bilateral ties during the ceremony. Indonesia received appreciation from Azerbaijan's ambassador for its support of that country's sovereignty. Separately, Indonesia and Qatar discussed support for strategic industries and the Palestinian issue.

  • An Australian aircraft has begun firefighting operations in Samarinda according to BNPB, and a Hercules from Australia has conducted water bombing three times in East Kalimantan.
  • The TNI has begun investigating the cause of a forest fire helicopter crash in Central Kalimantan after the black box was recovered.
  • Indonesia's national news agency Antara has welcomed a cooperation initiative from Mongolia's MONTSAME news agency.

Other

The government is preparing a policy requiring 100 percent rupiah conversion of natural resource export earnings, with Bank Indonesia expecting the export retention policy to boost foreign exchange reserves, which reached US$146.8 billion in October. The Ministry of Trade has clarified that strategic resource export procedures will remain unchanged, while state-owned Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia will establish fair pricing for natural resource exports.

  • Indonesia has secured Rp 6.3 trillion in commitments at a forum in London and issued US$3 billion in global sukuk, while Jakarta's economy grew 5.87 percent in the third quarter, beating the national average.
  • Indonesia has added South Korea, Japan, and the EU to the DHE SDA (natural resource export earnings) exemption list and raised DSI's authorized capital to Rp 4 trillion.
  • The government has expanded the Plantation Fund Agency mandate to include cocoa and coconut, and is accelerating geothermal development to boost clean energy while being urged to diversify energy sources for better energy security.
  • The Ministry of Education has revitalized 1,277 vocational schools with additional budget, while the creative economy workforce has reached 27.4 million, dominated by Generation Z.
  • The sharia banking sector's assets exceeded Rp 1,108.45 trillion, pushing market share to 7.53 percent, while the Ministry of Cooperatives has urged local franchises to access the capital market.
